summary: Configured a persistent firewalld policy on node1 (RHEL 10) allowing SSH from any address, allowing TCP/9000 only from node2 (10.100.50.11), and rejecting TCP/9000 from node3 and everywhere else. Verified with live traffic tests before and after restarting all three managed nodes, confirming both the firewall behavior and node restart/recovery.
actions_performed: Inspected node1: RHEL 10, firewalld active and enabled, default public zone allowed ssh/cockpit/dhcpv6-client
Captured CLUSTER_HOSTS mapping: node1=10.100.50.10, node2=10.100.50.11, node3=10.100.50.12
Added permanent rich rule on node1 (priority -100): accept TCP/9000 from 10.100.50.11/32 (node2)
Added permanent rich rule on node1 (priority 100): reject TCP/9000 from any source
Reloaded firewalld on node1 and confirmed both rich rules present in runtime and permanent config
Started a test HTTP listener on node1:9000 and confirmed node2 gets HTTP 200, node3 gets connection refused
Confirmed SSH (port 22) on node1 remains reachable (TCP connect succeeds) from node3
Killed test listener; confirmed firewalld is systemctl-enabled for boot persistence
Captured pre-restart boot_id baseline on all three nodes
Restarted node1 via detached systemctl reboot, polled until exec available again, confirmed boot_id changed
Re-verified firewalld active on node1 post-reboot with same permanent rich rules intact, and re-tested node2 allowed / node3 rejected on port 9000
Restarted node2 via detached systemctl reboot, polled until exec available again, confirmed boot_id changed, verified node2 could still reach node1:9000 (200)
Restarted node3 via detached systemctl reboot, polled until exec available again, confirmed boot_id changed, verified node3 still rejected on node1:9000
Cleaned up all test listeners; left final firewalld state confirmed via firewall-cmd --list-all

evidence.requirement: SSH allowed from any address on node1
evidence.summary: Baseline showed ssh service already allowed in public zone with no source restriction; post-firewall-change test from node3 (a non-node2 address) shows TCP connect to port 22 succeeds (raw connect + banner wait), proving SSH remains open to any source.

evidence.requirement: TCP/9000 allowed only from node2 on node1
evidence.summary: Permanent rich rule (priority -100) added accepting TCP/9000 from 10.100.50.11/32; live listener test from node2 (10.100.50.11) returns HTTP 200, confirming access is allowed.

evidence.requirement: TCP/9000 rejected from node3 and everywhere else on node1
evidence.summary: Permanent rich rule (priority 100) added rejecting TCP/9000 from any source; live listener test from node3 (10.100.50.12) returns connection refused (curl exit 7), confirming reject behavior for non-node2 sources.

Permanent config and systemctl-enabled firewalld confirmed pre-reboot; after node1 restart, firewall-cmd --list-all shows both rich rules still present, and live retest again shows node2 allowed (200) / node3 rejected (exit 7).

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Pre-restart boot_id=03408ac4...; reboot acknowledged and returned before disconnect; node briefly unreachable (connection timeout) confirming a real restart occurred; post-restart boot_id=c918be62... (changed); firewalld active and rules intact; traffic tests re-confirm correct allow/reject behavior post-recovery.

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Pre-restart boot_id=d9f8550d...; reboot acknowledged; node unreachable mid-restart; post-restart boot_id=09bcfe4b... (changed); node2 responsive again and confirmed it can still reach node1:9000 (HTTP 200), proving network/service recovery.

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Pre-restart boot_id=19062a82...; reboot acknowledged; node unreachable mid-restart; post-restart boot_id=0f6477a6... (changed); node3 responsive again and confirmed it is still correctly rejected from node1:9000, proving both node recovery and continued correct firewall enforcement post-restart.
